reason: IMPORTANT: App.razor is the top-level HTML document shell (html/head/body), rendered before the Blazor app itself mounts inside <body> - the same category as Boot.razor. The skip-link anchor is static host markup outside the composed component tree, not page content.

The ungrouped dashboard link sits in a bare <ul> so it lines up with the SiteNavGroup lists below it; SiteNavGroup itself requires a label, and a labelled group for a single top-level link would be wrong hierarchy. Same shape the public SiteSidebar uses for its home/about entries.

Bare <li> required because SiteNavGroup already renders the parent <ul> and expects list items as children; the child SiteNavLink already composes the interactive control. SiteListItem does not fit here because it renders a list-group row (used for search-result-style listings), without the nav-link/sidebar-action classes or AriaCurrent handling SiteNavLink already provides for sidebar navigation.

The <footer> landmark's own scoped CSS (SiteFooter.razor.css, including .site-main-scroll > .site-footer) is written against this file's Blazor CSS-isolation scope. Portfolio.Blazor.UI/Templates/SiteAppShell.razor only exposes a @Footer RenderFragment slot and does not itself render a <footer> element, so no existing Site* landmark wrapper can host this tag without relocating the scoped stylesheet. Verified: SiteAppShell.razor has no footer element; grep of *.css shows 12 rules keyed off .site-footer.

Global navigation shell rendered on every page (<aside>/<nav> landmarks plus a nav-item <ul>/<li> tree with active-state and nested-children logic that SiteListItem's fixed Outline/list-group shape cannot express, and an <hr> divider with no SiteDivider equivalent in Portfolio.Blazor.UI yet). Converting it safely requires adding new design-system primitives (landmark aside/nav wrappers, a divider, a nav-tree list item) plus full visual regression on every route, given its blast radius. Deliberately deferred to a dedicated follow-up rather than rushed; flagged as a task for the design-system library.

The right half of the same global navigation shell as SiteSidebar.razor, split out only to keep each file under the component-complexity budget; it carries the identical exemption and the identical follow-up (landmark section wrapper and nav-tree list item primitives in Portfolio.Blazor.UI). Merging it back would breach the complexity gate, so the exemption travels with the extracted half.
JS-interop host for the Cytoscape graph (see wwwroot/js/knowledge-map.js, loaded from App.razor): every div/span here is a DOM mount point selected by data-kmap-* hooks, not composed layout content.
Purely decorative, empty spinner glyph (aria-hidden) with no text content - not structural or content markup; no Site* primitive exists for a bare decorative icon-less spinner span.

Dynamic label spans read and rewritten by content-actions.js (data-content-actions-*-label hooks for progressive-enhancement copy/share state). SiteText's inline branch only covers fixed semantic variants (Eyebrow/SectionLabel/Meta/MetricLabel) and isn't meant for arbitrary JS-driven inline labels.
Host element required by the pax.BlazorChartJs ChartComponent to mount the underlying Chart.js canvas; this is a third-party interop boundary, not composed layout.

JS-interop tool (wwwroot/js referenced via data-color-wheel-* hooks) driving a <canvas>/<svg> color wheel, swatch grid, and contrast/colorblindness simulations directly in the DOM; not composable server-rendered markup.
JS-interop tool: data-flowchart-chart is a DOM mount point for the client-side flowchart-rendering script, not composed layout content.
JS-interop tool: the swatch div is a DOM mount point written to directly by the color-picker script after canvas pixel sampling, not composed layout content.
JS-interop host: table-editor.js mounts a spreadsheet widget into this element by id; not composed layout content.
data-file-panel/data-file-id hooks are toggled directly by client-side script to switch between snippet file tabs; the wrapping divs are JS-managed visibility panels, not composed layout content.

Bare decorative aria-hidden dot with no text content and no icon glyph - SiteBadge always renders label text and SiteIcon always renders a specific glyph, neither fits a plain decorative status dot; no Site* primitive exists for this shape.

CSV headers are only known at runtime (parsed from the uploaded file), so the column set can't be expressed with SiteDataTable's compile-time-typed SiteColumn API. Raw thead/tr/th/tbody/tr/td is the only way to render a dynamic-column table today; a generic dynamic-table component is a separate design task.

Same dynamic-column limitation as the paired <thead> row above - CSV columns are runtime-determined, not compile-time-known, so SiteDataTable's SiteColumn API does not apply.

Spreadsheet columns are user-defined at runtime (added/removed/reordered in the editor), so the column set can't be expressed with SiteDataTable's compile-time-typed SiteColumn API. Raw tbody/tr/td is the only way to render a dynamic-column table today; a generic dynamic-table component is a separate design task.

Non-interactive (SSR/print) fallback grid for a matrix, which has no column or row headers. SiteDataTable always renders a <thead>; converting would add a visible blank header row, a real visual regression. Raw tbody/tr/td keeps the headerless grid faithful.

IMPORTANT: the static fallback renders an N x N matrix whose column count is only known at runtime, which SiteDataTable's typed Columns API cannot express; the rows stay raw <tr>/<td> inside SiteTable's caption/scroll chrome.
